verdicts: Most direct evidence: NYC's extra staff are in track, station and signal upkeep.
Fits the maintenance-heavy staffing; cannot be tested separately with this data.
Admin rose from 13% of cost (2019) to 23% (2024).
About 7% of operating cost; at most about a quarter of the gap.
Hurts reliability and blocks crew savings; direct cost effect not separable.
London is older and cheaper; Chicago is old and cheap.
Fare recovery looks like a result of low cost and crowding, not a cause.
gaps: Paris: no metro-only cost is published (RATP reports metro, RER, tram and bus together).
Shanghai, Istanbul: no usable unit cost. Beijing: one news-report figure. Berlin: one cost per trip (2017).
Hong Kong, Seoul, Madrid and Singapore costs are estimates; Seoul 2022–24 is weak.
London car-km and Tokyo passenger-km after 2018 are estimated.
NYC data before 2012 is missing; 2012 and 2016–17 may be series breaks.
No foreign wage data, so "too many staff" and "staff paid too much" cannot be fully separated.
